follow-up time: Duration of hospitalization (up to one year)
outcome: Neonatal outcomes (live birth, abortion, stillbirth, neonatal death)
cohort: 62 pregnant women hospitalized for acute kidney injury (AKI)
finding: Acute kidney injury during pregnancy is associated with significant maternal and neonatal morbidity, with puerperal sepsis and preeclampsia/eclampsia being the most common causes.
mod_finding: The study found that the most common modes of delivery in women who developed AKI were normal vaginal delivery (51.6%) and lower segment cesarean section (33.9%).
